dedupe_keys.name: gecco industrial challenge 2019 drinking water quality time series for online event detection thuringer fernwasserversorgung

description: This dataset holds the real-world drinking water quality measurements used in the 2019 GECCO Industrial Challenge, a competition to build anomaly detection algorithms that flag undesirable changes in water quality with very low false alarm rates. It was organised by the SPOTSeven Lab at TH Köln and published on Zenodo by Steffen Moritz, Frederik Rehbach and Thomas Bartz-Beielstein, with data from the German bulk water supplier Thüringer Fernwasserversorgung and the IMProvT research project. Coverage: time series from one measuring station, split chronologically into training, test and validation sets, with the test period following the training period and validation following test; the challenge was based on a similar 2018 edition. Format and access: CSV files (training, test, validation and all merged, about 18 MB in total) plus the call for participation, rules and the participant resource package, openly downloadable from Zenodo record 4304080. Licence: CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: a single station, so it cannot represent network-wide behaviour; the measured parameters and the event labelling were not read here because the data files and rules PDF were not opened, and the Zenodo web page answered 403 so metadata came from the Zenodo API. Simulation uses: training and benchmarking water quality anomaly detectors for digital twins of drinking water systems and for emergency response to contamination events. Related records: the BATADAL datasets (data-batadal-attack-detection-datasets) are a comparable detection benchmark for water distribution networks.
